minutes.headline: Selectmen set a single tax rate, warned a pizzeria and Baker's, and backed the APDC's draft regulations.
minutes.summary: The board held a tax classification hearing and kept a single rate. It heard two liquor license matters (a hearing rescheduled and a warning issued to a variety store), approved a Salvation Army boot drive, and adopted updated designer selection procedures. It heard the Architectural Preservation District Commission's draft guidelines and recommended adoption despite a resident's objections. It went into executive session on union negotiations.

what_happened.line: The Select Board held its tax classification hearing and moved to keep a single tax rate for FY2018; the vote count was not audible.
The board recommended that the Architectural Preservation District Commission adopt its draft regulations and guidelines, with a clarified reference to the bylaw, after a resident objected.
The board found a license violation at Baker's Whale Variety and issued a warning as the penalty.
The board adopted designer selection procedures and approved a Salvation Army boot drive for December 9th; the vote counts were not audible.
The board rescheduled a pizzeria license violation hearing to December 5th, then went into executive session on collective bargaining.

why_it_matters: A single tax rate means homes and businesses are taxed at the same rate, so the classification vote bears directly on how the levy is split in a resident's FY2018 tax bill.
The APDC regulations cover building features such as temporary buildings, sliding doors, siding and metal roofs, so they may affect what owners in the preservation district can build or change.
watch_next: December 5th: the rescheduled pizzeria license violation hearing, and a possible economic development workshop.
December 19th: the regular meeting, where the consultant's economic development findings are planned to be presented.

They differ on the APDC recommendation vote, which only our minutes record, and on the Special Town Meeting positions and workshop date, which they describe differently.
